Ok, so I am going to build a dam/pond. Let me give you some backstory so you guys know what Im getting myself into. I am acquiring a winter draw water right for storage off of a local creek in Western Oregon. This means that I can fill my reservoir from the creek in the winter /spring and then can store the water for agricultural use throughout the year. I am the land owner, not some experienced contractor. Oh! and heres one better! I'm completely a novice at all this!

I have at my disposal a bobcat T550 with a toothed bucket which I plan on doing all the work with. I also have a laser level that will shoot a level line about 150 feet away with the sensor pole thing. It works really dam good (kek) as I used it to build 1600 feet of on-contour swale and burms last year and they were perfectly level. The property has a significant clay layer about 2-3 meters below the surface level (silty clay soil) that I have never managed to dig through. My hand powered rotary post hole digger just won't cut through the clay after about 1-2 meters. there is at least a meter of clay and probably more than that. The clay is really pure stuff. When it is dug out it is really shiny and really solid. It looks like it could be slapped on a potters wheel right out of the ground and function. There are almost no root penetration of any kind. I hope to move the top and subsoil away from this clay with my skidsteer, across the whole pond. dig into the clay and use it to build the interior key-way of the dam packing it with the machine as I go and then cover it with subsoil and rock (do I need to do rock?) Oh and it will probably have a slight outward curve if that makes any difference.

There is no requirement for engineering or building permits as long as I stay smaller than certain dimensions which I am. I am hoping to put about 5 acre feet of water behind this dam. It should have very minimal surface flow into it as it is up in a farm field as opposed to across a valley. There is some spring-type seepage that wells up in the area though during the wetter parts of the year which may deliver a bit of water into the system.

Anyone ever done this before? What are the most likely newbie-fuckups that I may fall into when getting into something like this?
